Fog-Aware Multi-Sensor Safety & Collision Risk 
Prediction System for Mine Vehicles
Proposed Solution:
FogGuard is an AI-powered multi-sensor safety system that improves mine-
vehicle awareness during dense fog by combining radar, camera, thermal, 
GNSS and IMU data.
➢Multi-sensor perception detects vehicles, people and obstacles beyond 
normal visibility. 
➢Sensor fusion combines radar and vision data for more reliable 
environmental awareness. 
➢Unknown-object handling identifies potential hazards even when the

➢Trajectory & risk prediction estimates collision possibility using distance,

Phantoms
Unique Value Proposition:
 Fog-Aware Fusion: Combines radar, camera & thermal sensing for reliable 
detection.
 Unknown-Object Safety: Detects unclassified obstacles as potential hazards.
 Predictive Risk:Uses distance, velocity & trajectory for early collision 
warnings.
 Onboard Intelligence: Processes sensor data locally for real-time alerts.
PROBLEM RESOLUTION:
❖ 3–5 m visibility in dense fog severely 
restricts dumper movement. 
❖ Camera-based detection becomes 
unreliable in extreme fog. 
❖ Reduced speed/stoppages increase haul-
cycle time and production losses. 
❖ Unknown obstacles like rocks and bends

Radar — Detects distance, angle & speed.

RGB Camera — Detects visible objects.

Edge AI — Processes sensor data locally.

mounted system.

faster detection and reducing dependence on continuous 
cloud connectivity.

Combining radar, camera and thermal data provides 
complementary information and improves object detection

The system can be designed as a modular safety layer that

connectivity is unavailable.
3.  Scalable & Upgradable
The system can support future upgrades such as 
V2V/V2I communication, mine-specific AI models and 
control-room integration.
4.  Safety & Operational Impact
Earlier detection and risk-based warnings can improve 
driver awareness, reduce collision risk and support 
safer haul-road operations in fog.

Provides real-time information about vehicles, people and

3.  Better Low-Visibility Perception:
Radar and thermal sensing complement cameras when 
normal visual detection becomes unreliable.
4.  Safer Mine Operations:
Supports safer movement of haul trucks and other vehicles 
on fog-affected mine roads.

instruction: Provide a comprehensive executive summary of the document '6333a80d-f588-40b9-ab02-85a7a439440a_Healthcare_Vending_Machine_Hackathon_Content _1_.pdf'. Include key takeaways, metrics, and risk factors.
input:
[Page 1]
MSME IDEA HACKATHON 6.0
Humanized English Content – AI-Powered Intelligent Healthcare Vending Machine with Automated Patient
Screening
Prepared from the uploaded hackathon document and the topic order shown in the provided form image.
1. Whether the idea involves use of existing intellectual property or not – give brief
detail
Length: 1012 / 1500 characters
The proposed innovation is an original integration of existing medical sensing, AI, IoT, payment,
medicine-dispensing, and automation technologies into one intelligent healthcare platform. The provided concept
does not identify any specific third-party patented or proprietary technology being directly adopted. Commercially
available devices such as blood-pressure monitors, thermometers, pulse-oximeters, heart-rate sensors, displays,
payment modules, and controllers can be used as building blocks. The main innovation is their integration into one
workflow covering patient interaction, basic screening, multilingual AI guidance, protocol-based medicine
recommendation, controlled dispensing, and, where clinically authorized, injection assistance. Before
commercialization, a formal patent/prior-art and freedom-to-operate search should be performed. Potentially
protectable elements may include the system architecture, software workflow, safety mechanism, or other
genuinely novel implementation features.
2. Briefly explain newness/uniqueness of the innovation
Length: 1097 / 1500 characters
The system goes beyond a conventional medicine vending machine by combining basic health assessment,
conversational AI, medicine dispensing, payment, and safety-oriented automation in one platform. It measures
parameters such as blood pressure, temperature, heart rate, and oxygen saturation while a multilingual AI voice
assistant records symptoms in simple language. The information can be evaluated using predefined, clinically
approved protocols to provide preliminary guidance and support authorized medicine dispensing. A further
differentiating feature is the proposed injection-assistance module, where a sensor-enabled chair verifies patient
positioning before an authorized automated procedure. The used syringe is then rendered unusable and routed to
designated biomedical-waste handling. This combination of multilingual interaction, integrated screening,
controlled dispensing, remote connectivity, and safety checks makes the platform more comprehensive than a
conventional vending machine. It is intended to support healthcare professionals, not replace diagnosis or
emergency care.
3. Concept & Objective
Length: 1063 / 1500 characters
The concept is to develop an AI-powered healthcare vending machine that provides first-level access to basic
healthcare services. The user selects a preferred language, describes symptoms through voice interaction, and
undergoes basic measurements using integrated medical devices. The system organizes the readings and
symptoms and evaluates them using predefined, clinically approved decision protocols. Based on the authorized
workflow, it can provide simple preliminary guidance and dispense permitted medicines after secure payment.
Where a doctor-authorized injectable treatment is supported, the safety module checks patient seating and other
predefined conditions before activation. The objective is to make basic healthcare support faster and easier to
access, particularly where healthcare staff are not immediately available. The system can also support remote
professional supervision, digital records where permitted, and multilingual assistance. Cases requiring professional
evaluation should be escalated rather than handled as automated diagnosis.
4. Specify the potential areas of application in industry/market in brief
Length: 1034 / 1500 characters
Potential deployment locations include government hospitals, Primary Health Centres, community health centres,
rural clinics, pharmacies, telemedicine centres, and private healthcare facilities. The kiosk can also be considered


[Page 2]
for corporate offices, manufacturing plants, colleges, universities, hostels, shopping malls, railway stations, bus
terminals, airports, metro stations, and other high-footfall locations. In underserved areas, it can support remote
healthcare networks by collecting basic health information and connecting users with healthcare professionals
when escalation is required. Other possible applications include disaster-relief camps, remote villages, industrial
sites, tourist locations, and elderly-care facilities. With appropriate regulatory approval and clinical supervision, the
platform can integrate with hospital information systems, electronic health records, telemedicine platforms, and
cloud-based monitoring services. Its modular architecture allows adaptation to different healthcare environments.
5. Briefly provide the market potential of the idea/innovation
Length: 1127 / 1500 characters
The proposed system has market potential because healthcare organizations are seeking digital solutions that
improve accessibility, reduce routine workload, and connect patients with healthcare services. A self-service kiosk
could support basic screening and guided primary-care services where demand is high or medical staff are limited.
Potential customers include government health departments, hospitals, pharmacy networks, corporate
organizations, educational institutions, transportation hubs, smart-city projects, NGOs, insurance-linked healthcare
programs, and telemedicine providers. Possible business models include kiosk sale or lease, annual maintenance
contracts, software subscriptions, remote monitoring, and authorized medicine-dispensing services. Further
opportunities may include system integration, analytics, and technical support, subject to healthcare and
pharmaceutical regulations. The platform can scale from a single kiosk to a connected healthcare network.
Commercial success will depend on clinical validation, regulatory compliance, patient

AI-Powered Intelligent Healthcare Vending Machine with Automated Patient Screening
9. Briefly explain
newness/uniqueness of
the innovation
The proposed innovation introduces an AI-Powered Intelligent Healthcare Vending Machine that delivers
primary healthcare services through a single automated platform. Unlike conventional medicine vending
machines, which only dispense medicines, this system first evaluates the patients health using integrated
medical devices such as a blood pressure monitor, digital thermometer, pulse oximeter, and heart rate
sensor. One of the key innovations is its multilingual AI voice assistant, which communicates with patients
in their preferred language. The assistant collects symptoms, explains the patients health condition in
simple terms, and provides preliminary healthcare guidance, making the system easy to use even for
people with limited medical knowledge. Based on the collected health data and approved medical
protocols, the system recommends suitable over-the-counter medicines or dispenses doctor-authorized
prescription medicines. The medicines are automatically dispensed after successful payment through UPI
or cash. Another distinctive feature is the smart injection assistance module. If an authorized injectable
medication is required, the patient sits on a sensor-enabled chair that checks for proper seating before
activating the automated syringe infusion system. This safety mechanism helps prevent incorrect
administration. Once the procedure is completed, the used syringe is automatically destroyed and safely
disposed of in a biodegradable biomedical waste.

10. Concept &
Objective
The main objective of this project is to develop an intelligent self-service healthcare kiosk that provides
quick, reliable, and affordable primary healthcare services with minimal human intervention. The system is
designed to assist people who need immediate basic medical support, especially in places where
healthcare professionals are not readily available. The machine integrates multiple medical devices to
measure essential health parameters such as body temperature, blood pressure, pulse rate, and oxygen
saturation. These readings are analyzed by an AI-powered voice assistant that interacts with patients in
their preferred language, understands their symptoms, and provides easy-to-understand health guidance.
Based on the assessment and approved medical protocols, the system recommends appropriate
medicines and dispenses them automatically after secure payment. When an authorized injectable
medicine is prescribed, the system verifies the patients seating position before operating the automated
syringe infusion mechanism, ensuring an additional layer of safety. After treatment, the syringe is
automatically destroyed and disposed of using a biomedical waste management system. The project aims
to improve healthcare accessibility, reduce waiting times in hospitals, support remote healthcare delivery,
and provide a reliable first point of medical assistance through an intelligent and fully integrated health.
11. Specify the
potential areas of
application in
industry/market in brief
The proposed healthcare vending machine has wide application across both public and private sectors
where immediate access to primary healthcare services is important. It can be installed in government
hospitals, Primary Health Centres (PHCs), community health centres, rural clinics, telemedicine centres,
and pharmacies to improve access to healthcare. The system is also suitable for corporate offices,
manufacturing industries, educational institutions, hostels, shopping malls, railway stations, bus terminals,
airports, metro stations, and other public locations where people may require immediate health
assessment and basic medical assistance. In addition, it can support healthcare services in disaster relief
camps, military bases, remote villages, tourist destinations, and elderly care facilities. The platform can
also be integrated with hospital information systems, electronic health records, and telemedicine networks,
allowing healthcare professionals to monitor patient data remotely and provide timely medical support.
With its modular design and multilingual capabilities, the solution can be adapted for different regions and
healthcare environments, making it suitable for large-scale deployment across India and other developing
countries.
12. Briefly provide the
market potential of
idea/innovation
The healthcare sector is rapidly adopting digital technologies to improve accessibility, reduce costs, and
enhance patient care. Increasing demand for primary healthcare services, along with shortages of
healthcare professionals in rural and underserved areas, creates a strong need for intelligent automated
healthcare solutions. The proposed AI-powered healthcare vending machine addresses this need by
offering 24×7 access to essential healthcare services through a compact and easy-to-use platform. It can
help reduce unnecessary hospital visits for minor illnesses, shorten patient waiting times, and support
healthcare providers by handling routine primary health assessments. Potential customers include

[Page 1]
MSME Proposal: AI-Powered Bone Fracture Detection System
I. Idea Theme
Artificial Intelligence–based diagnostic solution for automated bone fracture detection from X-ray
images. A cost-effective, accessible, and accurate medical tool bridging the gap in healthcare
availability, especially for rural and underserved regions.
II. Title of the Proposed Idea / Innovation
Design and Development of an AI-Powered, Low-Cost Bone Fracture Detection System for Rural
and Urban Healthcare
III. Introduction
Bone fractures are among the most common injuries worldwide, requiring timely diagnosis for
effective treatment. However, manual fracture detection from X-rays is time-consuming, prone to
human error, and heavily dependent on trained radiologists—who are often unavailable in rural and
low-resource settings. The project titled 'AI-Powered Bone Fracture Detection System' proposes the
development of a machine learning–based diagnostic tool that uses Convolutional Neural Networks
(CNNs) to detect fractures automatically from X-ray images. This system aims to provide fast,
accurate, and cost-effective diagnosis support, with the added advantage of offline functionality for
remote areas with limited internet access.
IV. Literature Survey
1. Rajpurkar et al. (2017): Developed CheXNet, a deep learning algorithm for chest X-rays,
achieving radiologist-level accuracy in pneumonia detection. 2. Olczak et al. (2020): Trained CNNs
on large orthopedic X-ray datasets and achieved over 90% accuracy in fracture detection. 3.
Bourouis et al. (2022): Proposed mobile-integrated AI healthcare systems that run on lightweight
devices. 4. Wong et al. (2021): Highlighted limitations of existing AI medical tools—high cost,
dependence on cloud servers, poor integration.
V. Problem Identification
1. Time-Consuming Diagnosis – Manual analysis of X-rays slows down treatment. 2. Risk of
Human Error – Fatigue and workload cause misdiagnosis. 3. Lack of Radiologists in Rural Areas –
Many clinics cannot afford specialists. 4. Delayed Treatment – Patients suffer due to late or missed
detection. 5. High Cost of Existing AI Solutions – Current tools are expensive and not designed for
small-scale or rural healthcare.
VI. Proposed Solution
We propose an AI-powered diagnostic tool that: - Automatically detects bone fractures from X-ray
images. - Runs both online (cloud servers) and offline (local mode). - Integrates seamlessly with
hospital systems (PACS/EHR). - Provides results in seconds, reducing diagnosis delays. - Offers a
lightweight, affordable, user-friendly interface that requires no specialist training.
VII. Methodology
1. Data Collection – Acquire diverse, annotated X-ray datasets. 2. Preprocessing – Perform
normalization, noise removal, and contrast adjustment. 3. Model Training – Train CNNs to classify
images as 'fracture' or 'no fracture.' 4. Validation & Testing – Validate against real hospital datasets
for reliability. 5. Deployment – Develop a cross-platform interface for clinicians. 6. Scalability –
Enable offline support for rural clinics and cloud support for urban hospitals.
VIII. Work Plan

X. Briefly Explain Newness/Uniqueness of the Innovation
Affordable AI tailored for rural clinics and small hospitals. Offline mode ensures usability in
low-connectivity areas. Lightweight interface requiring no extra specialist training. Scalable design
adaptable to other diagnostic conditions (arthritis, pneumonia, cancers). Directly addresses gaps in
existing costly AI solutions.
XI. Concept & Objective
Concept: To create an AI-based diagnostic tool that bridges the gap between medical expertise and
accessibility. Objectives: - Automate X-ray–based fracture detection. - Improve accuracy and
reduce diagnostic delays. - Support both online and offline modes. - Provide a user-friendly
interface for clinicians. - Enhance healthcare accessibility in underserved regions.
XII. Potential Areas of Application
- Hospitals, diagnostic labs, and emergency units. - Rural healthcare centers and mobile clinics. -
Telemedicine platforms and NGOs. - Military, disaster relief, and trauma care. - International
adoption in emerging markets.
XIII. Market Potential
The global AI in healthcare market is rapidly expanding. In India, government initiatives like
Ayushman Bharat and the National Digital Health Mission encourage AI integration in diagnostics.
Primary customers: Hospitals, labs, radiologists. Secondary customers: Rural clinics, NGOs,
telemedicine providers. End users: Orthopedic specialists, trauma centers, patients. This solution
has high potential due to low cost, scalability, and offline compatibility, making it suitable for both
urban and rural healthcare markets.
